reference.title: Dumbbell Incline Fly
reference.listing: Video; data sheet: body part Chest, equipment Dumbbell, exercise type Strength
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

breathing.pattern: Inhale as the arms open, exhale as you squeeze them back together.
breathing.cadence: About 2.2 s down, 0.4 s stretch, 1.5 s up

prescription.tempo: 3-1-2-0 (3 s down, 1 s stretch, 2 s up)
prescription.load: Dumbbell load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can lift for the target reps with 1-3 reps in reserve (RIR 1-3, about RPE 7-9). Use much lighter dumbbells than for the press.
prescription.progression: More reps, then a slower lowering, then the next dumbbell.

cues.text: Set the back pad to 30 degrees, glutes in the crease, upper back and head on the pad, feet planted; dumbbells together over the upper chest, palms facing each other, elbows softly bent.
Breathe in and open the arms in a wide arc, elbows softly bent and fixed, like hugging a big tree in reverse.
Stop when the upper arms are about level with the bench and the chest is stretched; palms face the ceiling.
Breathe out and squeeze the chest to sweep the dumbbells back up along the same arc.
Bring the dumbbells together over the chest without letting them touch; keep the elbow bend.

mistakes.mistake: Turning the fly into a press (elbows bending and straightening)
mistakes.fix: Fix a soft bend in the elbows at the top and keep that same angle all the way down and up.
Stop when the upper arms are about level with the bench and you feel a stretch across the chest, not a pull in the front of the shoulder.
Keep a soft bend (elbows at about 150-160 degrees) to keep the load off the elbow joint.
The fly needs a much lighter dumbbell than the press; in one study the 6-repetition maximum was less than half the bench press load (Solstad 2020).

mistakes.mistake: Clanging the dumbbells at the top
mistakes.fix: Bring them together in a wide hug and stop just before they touch; squeeze the chest.

kinematics.norm: Back pad at 30 degrees, seat flat (same angle as the incline press: 30 degrees maximised upper-pectoralis activity in pressing, Rodríguez-Ridao 2020; no incline fly study found)
Fixed soft bend: Solstad 2020 held the elbow at about 150-160 degrees (20-30 degrees of flexion) at the bottom and stopped the set if it bent further
From over the chest to about level with the bench at the bottom (clinical opinion); Solstad 2020 standardised depth with the dumbbell bands touching the chest line
Upper arms about level with the bench at the bottom, no lower (clinical opinion)
Neutral: palms face each other at the top and the ceiling at the bottom (clinical opinion)
Feet flat, knees about 90 degrees (Solstad 2020 set-up)
Slow and controlled; Solstad 2020 used a controlled self-selected tempo. About 2-3 s down and 1.5-2 s up (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #031912, Dumbbell Incline Fly, video (movement reference)

Solstad, Andersen, Shaw, Hoel, Vonheim and Saeterbakken 2020, a comparison of muscle activation between barbell bench press and dumbbell flyes in resistance-trained males (J Sports Sci Med 19(4):645-651; PMC7675616)

Rodríguez-Ridao, Antequera-Vique, Martín-Fuentes and Muyor 2020, effect of five bench inclinations on the electromyographic activity of the pectoralis major, anterior deltoid and triceps brachii during the bench press exercise (Int J Environ Res Public Health 17(19):7339; PMC7579505)
Lauver, Cayot and Scheuermann, influence of bench angle on upper extremity muscular activation during bench press exercise (Eur J Sport Sci, 2016; PubMed 25799093)

cautions: Get into position safely: sit on the end of the bench with the dumbbells on the thighs, then lie back and kick them up one knee at a time; at the end of the set bring them back to the thighs or lower them to the floor beside the bench rather than dropping them (clinical opinion).
Shoulder pain: shorten the range at the bottom and keep the upper arms out of the fully stretched position until it settles (clinical opinion).
Keep the wrists straight over the forearms; bent-back wrists under a heavy dumbbell strain the wrist.
Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Do not let heavy dumbbells pull the arms below the bench line: the stretched shoulder is the vulnerable position (clinical opinion).
modify: Shoulder discomfort: shorten the arc so the upper arms stop above the bench line.
Elbow discomfort: keep a little more bend and use lighter dumbbells.
regressions: Floor fly (the floor limits the depth).
Machine pec deck or band fly.
progressions: Slower lowering with a 1-2 s pause in the stretch.
Cable fly (more tension at the top).

muscleNotes.pec_r: Main mover (horizontal adduction), biased toward the upper fibres by the incline: in pressing, 30 degrees gave the highest upper-pectoralis activity (Rodríguez-Ridao 2020); the fly itself has been studied flat, where it was about 16% below the barbell bench press overall (Solstad 2020).
muscleNotes.pec_l: Main mover (horizontal adduction), biased toward the upper fibres by the incline: in pressing, 30 degrees gave the highest upper-pectoralis activity (Rodríguez-Ridao 2020); the fly itself has been studied flat, where it was about 16% below the barbell bench press overall (Solstad 2020).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Helps bring the arms together; it works harder as the bench rises (Rodríguez-Ridao 2020, pressing).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_l: Helps bring the arms together; it works harder as the bench rises (Rodríguez-Ridao 2020, pressing).
muscleNotes.biceps_r: Holds the fixed elbow bend against the load: biceps activity was about 76% higher in the dumbbell fly than in the bench press (Solstad 2020).
muscleNotes.biceps_l: Holds the fixed elbow bend against the load: biceps activity was about 76% higher in the dumbbell fly than in the bench press (Solstad 2020).
muscleNotes.serratus_r: Keeps the shoulder blades on the rib cage while the arms open and close.
muscleNotes.serratus_l: Keeps the shoulder blades on the rib cage while the arms open and close.
muscleNotes.triceps_r: Light work holding the elbows from bending further; about 75% lower than in the bench press (Solstad 2020).
muscleNotes.triceps_l: Light work holding the elbows from bending further; about 75% lower than in the bench press (Solstad 2020).
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_r: Grip the handles, palms facing each other.
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_l: Grip the handles, palms facing each other.
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_r: Rotator cuff: steadies the head of the upper arm in the stretched position (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_l: Rotator cuff: steadies the head of the upper arm in the stretched position (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.core: Bracing keeps the ribs down and the pelvis on the seat.
